::: {.callout-important}
VU Amsterdam advises researchers to no longer start new projects in OSF. The project functionality will cease to work as of **19 February 2027**. Any projects expected to be active at that time will have to move to alternative tools in order to keep sharing research documents with colleagues. 
https://www.cos.io/osf-changes
https://www.cos.io/blog/osf-changes-a-note-to-users?hsLang=en

The OSF pre-registration and pre-print functionality will remain unchanged.

For further information, contact: [osfadmin@vu.nl](mailto:osfadmin@vu.nl)
:::

## What is it?

The [Open Science Framework](https://osf.io/) (OSF) is a cloud-based open-source preprint and preregistration tool that supports researchers throughout the active research stage. The OSF is developed by the [Center of Open Science (COS)](http://cos.io/) that strives to increase openness, integrity, and reproducibility of research. This is in line with the [VU open science commitment](https://vu.nl/en/about-vu/organisations/open-science) where the aim is to make the process of creating and sharing scientific knowledge more transparent, inclusive and equitable.

## What can it be used for?

OSF can be used during the active research stage. It can be used for preregistration or preprints:

1.  [Preregistration of your research ideas - OSF Support](https://help.osf.io/article/145-preregistration).

2.  Preprints: OSF can also be used to publish your preprints. See the manual [Creating a Preprint - OSF Support](https://help.osf.io/article/399-creating-a-preprint), which describes in seven steps how you can publish a preprint. Please note that you have to submit it to a [community preprint service](https://help.osf.io/article/686-preprint-services). You can select a preprint service that matches best with your discipline. When your preprint is approved, it will be linked to VU Amsterdam and listed in the [VU preprint overview on OSF](https://osf.io/institutions/vua?resourceType=Preprint).
